headline: Haleakala and Waianapanapa Reservation Requirements
reservation: National Park sunrise access and entry to Waianapanapa State Park require advance reservations for out-of-state visitors. These systems are independent and often book weeks in advance; check official NPS and Hawaii State Parks websites for current release schedules and permit availability.

days.title: Volcanic Summits and High Elevation

stops.name: Haleakala Visitor Center
stops.detail: Ascend to nearly 10,000 feet to view the vast volcanic basin and unique alpine ecosystem.

stops.name: Hosmer Grove
stops.detail: Walk the short nature trail to see native honeycreepers and high-altitude flora.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours for the ascent; steep grades and switchbacks require cautious driving.
days.note: Temperatures at the summit are significantly lower than the coast; bring warm layers.

days.title: The Windward Rainforest Journey

stops.name: Waianapanapa State Park
stops.detail: Explore the black sand beach and volcanic sea arches; ensure you have a confirmed reservation.

stops.name: Hana Town
stops.detail: Stop for local provisions and appreciate the quiet pace of this remote coastal community.

days.driving: Allow 3 to 5 hours for the Road to Hana; travel time depends on stops and bridge traffic.
days.note: Flash floods can occur in windward valleys; check weather before entering stream beds.

days.title: Coastal Heritage and Marine Life

stops.name: Maui Ocean Center
stops.detail: Learn about Hawaii's coral reefs and marine conservation in an established educational setting.

stops.name: Kapalua Coastal Trail
stops.detail: Walk the rocky shoreline path for views of Molokai and seasonal whale watching from the cliffs.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours; traffic between South and West Maui can be heavy during commute times.
days.note: Whale sightings are seasonal, typically peaking between December and April.

intel.title: Park Entry Constraints
intel.text: Parking at Haleakala summit overlooks and Waianapanapa is strictly controlled. Arriving without a reservation during restricted hours will result in turned-away entry.

intel.title: Hana Highway Dead Zones
intel.text: Cellular service is non-existent along large stretches of the Road to Hana and within Haleakala's backcountry. Offline GPS data is necessary for navigation.

intel.title: Strategic Refueling
intel.text: Gas is readily available in Central Maui and Kihei but limited to a single station in Hana. Fill your tank in Kahului or Paia before starting long mountain or coastal drives.

intel.title: Early Starts
intel.text: Trade winds and cloud cover typically increase in the afternoon. Schedule summit visits and snorkeling for the early morning hours for the best visibility.

intel.title: Regional Weather
intel.text: Conditions can be sunny in Kihei while heavy rain falls in Hana. Consult the Hawaii Department of Transportation for road closures due to landslides or high surf.

plan.arrival: Collect your rental at OGG and stock up on supplies in Kahului before heading to your regional base in Kihei or Lahaina.
plan.vehicle: A standard car is suitable for main roads; check rental contracts for restrictions on the 'back road' from Hana.
plan.goldenHour: The Haleakala summit provides a vantage point for sunset above the clouds, though wind-chill is severe after dark.
